units.en: For naval technology without ⟦0⟧, see the separate ⟦1⟧ page.

⟦0⟧ replaces the existing ⟦1⟧ system of set, successive designs with an extensive modular system that allows players to create more highly customized individual ship classes. Each ship has a number of slots for modules depending on its hull type, located above and below its portrait in the ship design screen. The bottom-side slots are considered fundamental mountings for the class and are universal to them, though some such as AA or torpedoes need not be filled. For instance, all destroyers have bottom-side mountings for one battery gun, one AA mount, a fire control/sonar, a sonar/radar, a torpedo launcher, and an engine. All ships also are required to have certain mountings -- a destroyer, for instance, must have a battery and an engine, as otherwise it has no means to move or defend itself.

However, the mountings above the portrait are additional slots for customizing the class, and contain no mandatory elements. These are divided into three sections for the ship -- front, middle, and rear, with up to two front and rear slots and three middles ones. As an example, the Early Destroyer only has one middle and one rear slot above-portrait, but the 1940 Destroyer has a middle, rear, and front.

Exactly what can go in the optional slots also changes from ship class to ship class. Cruisers and battleships can only mount main guns or AA in their front slots, but destroyers can mount depth charges in theirs (as the 1940 technology bracket also unlocks the Depth Charge Mortar). A wide variety of equipment exists that can produce highly specialized ships.
With the introduction of special projects in ⟦0⟧ and the accompanying ⟦1⟧, all naval technologies now also generate naval engineering breakthrough progress while being researched.

Basic Depth ChargesA simple explosive container with a pressure-sensitive trigger explodes when it hits a pre-set depth. Mounting this module on Light Ships and Cruisers will allow them to attack enemy Submarines.
Unlocks Depth Charge Rails Depth charges: 8.0 Max speed: -1% Production cost: 90.00

Depth Charge ThrowerA simple mechanical device that tosses a depth charge a set distance away from the ship. This means that the destroyer no longer has to drive directly across the target to hit it. Mounting this module on Light Ships and Cruisers will allow them to attack enemy Submarines.
Unlocks Depth Charge Thrower Depth charges: 13.0 Max speed: -1% Production cost: 120.00

Depth Charge MortarA mortar on board the destroyer can throw an explosive charge much further, allowing the ship to maintain sonar contact with the submarine throughout the attack and dramatically increasing its accuracy. Mounting this module on Light Ships and Cruisers will allow them to attack enemy Submarines.
Unlocks Anti-submarine Mortar Depth charges: 17.0 Max speed: -2% Production cost: 150.00

Improved Depth Charge MortarA larger propellant charge throws a proper depth charge set to a specific depth at a submarine from quite a distance. Mounting this module on Light Ships and Cruisers will allow them to attack enemy Submarines.
Unlocks Advanced Anti-submarine Mortar Depth charges: 22.0 Max speed: -2% Production cost: 180.00
Smoke GeneratorsSome minor modifications to the engines and smokestacks of light and medium ships allow them to make a lot of smoke to avoid or break contact with the enemy.
Global stats Fleet speed while retreating: +20%

Passive SonarA basic set of hydrophones allows tracking of underwater targets through detecting the sound they make. Mounting this module in an Electronics Slot on Light Ships or Cruisers will help them detect enemy Submarines.
Unlocks Hydrophones Sub detection: 8.0 Production cost: 40.00

Active SonarUsing modulated sound waves, this system can accurately measure bearing and distance to a submerged target. Mounting this module in an Electronics Slot on Light Ships or Cruisers will help them detect enemy Submarines.
Unlocks Active Sonar Sub detection: 12.0 Production cost: 60.00
